content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} motor vehicle sales tax on the price less a trade-in. Yearly registration tax is a share of the vehicle's original sticker price that falls as it ages.

howItWorks.text: The sales tax is a percentage of the taxable sales price. A motor vehicle traded in comes off the price first.
If you paid tax to a state that gives a similar credit, {state} charges only the difference in rates.
Registration tax is ten dollars plus a share of the sticker price. The share is highest in the first year and drops each year until it reaches a flat amount.
Title, filing, technology and transfer fees are charged on each title transaction.

faq.q: Why is {state} registration higher for a new vehicle?
faq.text: The registration tax is a share of the original sticker price, and the share is largest in the first year of the vehicle's life.

faq.q: Is there local tax on a vehicle in {state}?
faq.text: Some counties and cities charge a flat twenty-dollar vehicle excise tax. There is no percentage local sales tax on the vehicle in the Department's guide.
